title: Choose the look for Big Rock Management
question: The dice dealt The Patch Collection. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Patch Collection
options.lineage: National-park patches, travel decals, and the Big Rock logo itself
options.thesis: Your logo is already a patch, so every company gets one, and the site is the collection board where visitors pick theirs.
materials: embroidered patch badges with a dark navy border
options.viewport: A big headline next to a cluster of four badges: Rentals, Service Solutions (cleaning), Hauling, and an empty stitched outline marked 'Realty, coming soon'. Each badge links to its page, and a 'Free quote' button sits in the nav.
options.risk: If the badges are drawn timidly, this turns into a merch page. They have to be bold and well made.

raised.raise: Every badge scene is built from flat, separately cut color layers (butte, saguaro, sun), with depth from overlap and no soft shading.
Each company owns one spot color pulled from the logo's sunset (gold for Hauling, coral for Cleaning, magenta for Rentals, violet for Realty), which carries its whole page.
What isn't live yet is drawn on purpose: the Realty badge is an empty stitched outline until that site launches.

options.label: Miracle Mile Motel Sign
options.lineage: Tucson's Miracle Mile neon motel signs (Ghost Ranch Lodge, Tucson Inn)
options.thesis: The site is a roadside motel sign: a big arrow, a lit VACANCY, and one panel per service.
options.viewport: A tall sign at dusk with BIG ROCK on the marquee, panels reading Rentals / Cleaning / Hauling / Realty, and a lit 'VACANCY: free quotes' button.
options.risk: This is also where most Tucson brands land, and it sits close to the Realty Group's neon look.

options.label: Annotated Job Photos
options.lineage: Japanese fashion mook spreads with hand-drawn label ribbons
options.thesis: Overlapping photos of real jobs, with hand-drawn ribbons naming everything in them: 'old sectional', 'yard brush', 'guest-ready linens'.
options.viewport: A stacked fan of photos (a haul trailer, a reset bedroom, a casita) with ribbons labeling each item, and the quote form folded in like an insert.
options.case: Holds up on clarity because the labels show exactly what you haul and clean. It loses on audience fit and depends on real photos you don't have yet.
options.risk: Until your own job photos arrive, stock images will make it feel generic.

options.label: Layered Papercut
options.thesis: A symmetrical cut-paper roundel, built up one color layer at a time.
options.viewport: A symmetrical roundel with the services cut as layers.
options.risk: Tucson owners won't recognize Polish folk art.
options.case: Loses on audience fit and clarity.
options.kept: Kept: depth from overlapping flat layers, with no shading.

options.label: Mid-century Magazine
options.thesis: A strict grid, one spot color per issue, and a hidden mark.
options.viewport: A serif masthead over two columns.
options.risk: Too editorial for a service business.
options.case: Loses on audience fit and clarity.
options.kept: Kept: each company owns one spot color.

options.label: Gas-Station Price Sign
options.lineage: Seven-segment LED signs and price totems
options.thesis: Services listed like gas prices, with unlit segments drawn on purpose.
options.viewport: A price-totem stack of the services.
options.case: Loses on clarity, because it suggests a price list.
options.kept: Kept: missing pieces are designed, not hidden.

options.label: WebGL Shader Portal
options.thesis: A full-screen animated shader with thin type floating over it.
options.viewport: One huge word over a living sunset field.
options.risk: Hides the services, and runs slowly on phones.
options.case: Loses on clarity and audience fit.
options.kept: Kept: one oversized word, set with confidence.

canonCard.label: Standard home-services site
canonCard.thesis: What local service companies usually ship, done with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A photo hero with a headline and quote button, three or four service cards, a 'why us' strip, and a quote form.
